text:
maya: hey team, ACME reports intermittent 502s and very slow token generation (~4-6s). they attached a screenshot but no trace id. asking what minimal bits we need to reproduce quickly

jordan: ask for the session hash + minimal curl and a screenshot of the Console request row. session hash is the fastest to correlate. :eyes:

maya: wrote back to customer: please send 1) the session hash (Console -> Activity -> click the row -> Copy session hash) 2) a minimal curl that reproduces the call (headers + payload) 3) a timestamp of when it happened 4) a screenshot of the request row showing latencies. also asked for any SDK logs if they were using web/mobile.

jordan: if they used our web SDK, tell them to open devtools and run: `console.log(window.__REDWOOD && window.__REDWOOD.session)` — that often prints the session hash. for native SDKs ask for the debug token or log snippet that contains `trace=` or `session=`.

maya: they replied: "we don't see a copy button, only an ID column" — so I told them to hover over the ID and right-click -> Copy, or click the three-dot menu on the request row and choose Copy ID. added screenshot link: https://img.redwood.fake/snip123

jordan: if copying from a proxy/edge, ask them to include the request header we insert: `X-RW-TRACE` (or any `x-rw-*` header). sample curl to ask them to paste back: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -H "X-RW-TRACE: <paste-from-response-or-logs>" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

maya: i also asked them to capture a HAR if it's a browser issue and to include the `Response headers` panel in the screenshot. gave them quick steps for HAR export in Chrome.

jordan: for mobile repros: Android = `adb logcat | grep -i redwood` and look for `trace=` or `session=`; iOS = attach device logs from Xcode or `idevicesyslog` and grep for `rw_trace`/`sessionhash`. tell them to mark the approximate timestamp in the logs.

maya: customer sent back a small curl but the header was missing. they gave us a proxy trace with `edge-span: a1b2c3`. i replied: good — edge-span helps, but we still need the internal session hash or the `X-RW-TRACE` value from the response headers to map to service spans. asked them to re-run with `-v` and paste the response headers.

jordan: if customer can't or won't run curl, ask them to copy the SDK request payload and the network tab row. even the request timestamp + request path + status code can let us find it.

maya: i also included a one-click debug bundle instruction: "Console -> Support -> Create debug bundle" and a short note: if using Dedicated/Private, run `rwctl debug generate --session <session-hash>` and paste the returned debug token.

support-bot: debug-bundle created (id: dbg-20240715-99) — Maya created a customer debug request.

jordan: once we have the session hash or X-RW-TRACE value, we can run an internal query to stitch spans and produce a flame graph. if latency is in model decode, we'll see token timing. if it's gateway, we'll see upstream retries.

maya: update for case: customer came back with session-hash `sh_7f9a` and a curl with `-v` headers. i forwarded both to eng-oncall and included timestamp. asking eng to triage.

jordan: triage notes: found span mapped to gateway -> auth token refresh -> model pool. gateway retried once due to transient 502 from pool; decode time was normal. recommended short-term: increase client retry window and add a canary to Dedicated routing. long-term: investigate pool health alerts during that window.

maya: replied to customer with root cause summary + suggested mitigations and asked them to reopen if it recurs. added checklist for support to avoid back-and-forth: 1) session hash or X-RW-TRACE 2) minimal curl with `-v` 3) timestamp (UTC) 4) screenshot of request row or HAR 5) SDK logs if native/mobile.

jordan: thanks — saving this checklist snippet to support runbook. :white_check_mark:
